views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold China's calibrated retaliatory tariffs in place as leverage but do not escalate further; signal readiness to negotiate during the window before either tariff set takes effect. Keep the ~$50B farm-belt counter-measures (soybeans, autos, aircraft) positioned and explicitly tie their activation to US actions, while opening talks on the Section 301 complaints without conceding on IP/tech-transfer structural demands.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is real but not yet existential. The Section 301 report (2018-03-22) and the proposed ~$50B/1,300-line list (2018-04-03) directly target the Made-in-China-2025 technology sectors (aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery) that underpin China's self-sufficiency ambitions — a genuine challenge warranting an above-neutral threat reading (+0.4). However, as of the decision date the tariffs are proposed, not imposed: the US comment window runs to May 22 with a hearing May 15, and China's own Finance officials stress the pre-implementation period is 'time to negotiate and cooperate.' China's macro is strong — industrial output up 7.2% y/y in Jan-Feb with PMI in expansion and a ~6.5% growth target — so there is no FX, credit, or employment crisis forcing a response. China's proportional $50B retaliation (2018-04-04) is deliberately aimed at politically sensitive US farm-belt exports to create domestic pressure on the administration, giving Beijing real leverage. Escalating further now would risk a mutually damaging spiral and undercut China's posture as defender of the multilateral trading order; conceding now would forfeit leverage with no US rollback on the table. Hence a mild action stance (-0.1) on the negotiate axis: keep retaliation as leverage, engage talks, reserve further measures for clarity on US intentions.
key_factors: Section 301 proposed $50B list targets Made-in-China-2025 sectors (aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery) — direct challenge to China tech autonomy
Neither US nor Chinese tariffs are in effect as of 2018-04-12; comment window to May 22 leaves negotiation space
China's matching $50B retaliation (2018-04-04) hits US farm belt (soybeans) to pressure Trump domestically
China macro robust (industrial output +7.2% y/y Jan-Feb, PMI expansion, ~6.5% growth target) — no FX/financial crisis
Both sides signal tariffs may never be imposed if talks succeed; window favors negotiation with leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (soybeans, automobiles, aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable; Trump directs tariffs, WTO case, investment restrictions.
China's response matched the ~$50B US proposal; implementation depends on US action; 'time to negotiate and cooperate' per Zhu Guangyao.
China industrial output up 7.2% y/y Jan-Feb 2018; healthy robust economy.
